Author: K. Suresh Reddy
Bench: K. Suresh Reddy
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Suresh Reddy
 Crl.R.C.NO.1073 Of 2022
Order:

Questioning the order passed by the Additional Junior Civil Judge-Cum-I Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Vizianagaram in Crl.M.P.No.6220 of 2018 in C.C.No.1670 of 2017 dated 21.06.2022, the petitioner filed the present Revision before this Court.

entities.text: Additional Junior Civil Judge-Cum-I Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Vizianagaram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case is that the petitioner and A1 were charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Section 467, 468, 471, 477-A and 420 read with 34 of IPC in Crime No.165 of 2014 of Vizianagaram Rural Police Station, Vizianagaram District in C.C.No.1670 of 2017.

entities.text: Vizianagaram Rural Police Station, Vizianagaram District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. The case of the prosecution is that A1 is the husband of the petitioner and A1 worked as Junior Assistant in the District Court, Vizianagaram from 13.06.2009 to 17.06.2013 and the petitioner is house wife.

The duties of A1 in respect of MVOP are preparation of cheques, contingent bills, budget observation, sending permission petitions to the Banks, receiving DDs and entering the same in D.D. receive register, preparation of challanas, maintaining ledger-38 & 39, account section miscellaneous correspondence and FDR registers maintenance etc.
4.
On 23.04.2013 L.W.5 filed a petition under Section 151 C.P.C in MVOP No.374 of 2007 before the Court praying to grant payment of Rs.50,321/- due to him.
The said petition was forwarded to the accounts section for verification by the District Court.

The accounts clerk verified the Fixed Deposit Receipt Register and found that the relevant entry shows that an amount of Rs.25,000/- is only recorded in the Fixed Deposit Receipt Register instead of Rs.50,321/- and informed the variation to the accounts section.

L.W.2 who verified the old cheque petitions and FDR ledgers and found that there are two FDRs and another FDR of Rs.1,30,321/- in favour of Indian Overseas Bank,
Vizianagaram.

The said amount of Rs.1,30,321/- was encashed on 05.12.2011 by the first accused and the amount of Rs.80,000/- was delivered to L.W.5 in the shape of Demand Draft as per cheque petition order No.588 of 2013 dated 23.04.2013.
Similarly, he has encashed various FDRs.
The total amount misappropriated by the A1 is Rs.10,87,448/-.
Most of the amounts misappropriated by the A1 has been deposited into the account of A2 who is petitioner herein.
The allegation made in the charge sheet is that A1 and A2 with their connivance and knowledge have deposited amounts into the account of A2, the petitioner.
As such, there is specific allegation against the petitioner also attributing connivance and knowledge.

CRLRC/1073/2022 on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126659085/
1 5.

Learned Counsel for the petitioner strenuously contends that the petitioner is none other than the wife of A1 and she does not have any knowledge about deposit of the said misappropriated amount by A1.
Petitioner is a house wife and she has no knowledge about the misappropriation.
As such, she filed a discharge petition under Section 239 Cr.P.C.
The Court below without perusing the contentions raised by the petitioner, dismissed the discharge application, which is impugned in the present Criminal Revision Petition.

6. On the other hand, learned Special Assistant Public Prosecutor contended that the allegations made in the charge sheet is that A1 and A2 have got common intention to misappropriate the money by forging the documents and created fictitious letters said to have been issued by the District Judge, Vizianagaram.

7. This Court perused the entire material on record as seen from the averments made in the charge sheet, prima facie there are allegations of common intention and as such, this is not a fit case for discharge and she can establish her innocence during the course of trial.
As such, this Court is not in a position to interfere with the orders passed by the Court below.
8. Accordingly, this Crl.R.C. is dismissed at the admission stage.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.

K. SURESH REDDY, J 21.07.2023 JLV/PGT HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K.
SURESH REDDY Dated: 21.07.2023 JLV/PGT CRLRC/1073/2022 on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126659085/
